up.sh runs `docker compose up -d --build --wait` and prints `site http://localhost:8080/`. docker-compose.yml: service web `image: caddy:2.10.0`, mounts `./www:/srv/www:ro`, shares the lab network which publishes `8080:8080`. Caddyfile: `:8080 { root * /srv/www ... handle { file_server } }`. Same at stage-1 (diff only removes stub API routes and adds reverse_proxy for /api/v1/*).

issues.quote: View source shows the original HTML text, which can differ from the DOM.
issues.text: Key (a) is correct and every distractor is wrong. Only the explanation keeps the view-source wording the lesson dropped in r1: Chrome asks the server again when view-source opens (claim 3), so it shows the HTML as the server sends it, not a stored 'original'. q2 explanation.correct ('the source text stays as it arrived') has the same slant.
issues.fix: q1 explanation.c: "View source shows the HTML as the server sends it, which can differ from the DOM." q2 explanation.correct: "...while the HTML the server sends stays the same." Update vi to match.

issues.quote: A new page load is what a plain link does, not what a script needs.
issues.text: Not in claims. True for a link to another page, but a link to a place on the same page (href="#...") does not load a new page. Low risk at this level; wording can be made exact at no cost.
issues.fix: "A new page load is what following a link to another page does, not what a script needs."

issues.quote: `body` holds nine elements: the `h1` heading, the `p` paragraph, the `ul` list, three `li` list items and three `a` links, one inside each item, plus their text.
issues.text: §3 just taught parent and child, so I read 'body holds nine elements' as body having nine children. Only on a second read do I see that the li items sit inside the ul and each a inside an li. I had to re-read to build the tree in my head.
issues.fix: Say which are direct children: "`body` holds the `h1` heading, the `p` paragraph and the `ul` list; the `ul` holds three `li` list items, each holding one `a` link, plus their text: nine elements in all."

issues.quote: Its DOM has `html` at the top, with the elements `head` and `body` under it.
issues.text: The tags h1, p, ul, li, a are now explained, but html, head and body are not, and the prereq summary does not name them. I can guess body is the visible part; I do not know what head is for.
issues.fix: Add a few words at first use: "with the elements `head` (information about the page, not shown) and `body` (what is shown on screen) under it".

issues.quote: the browser tidies the HTML as it builds, for example by closing a paragraph the author left open.
issues.text: 'a paragraph the author left open' assumes I know elements have an opening and a closing tag; neither the lesson nor the prereq summary says that. I get the general idea (the browser fixes mistakes) but not the example.
issues.fix:
Make the example self-explaining: "for example by adding the closing `

` an author forgot to write after a paragraph".

issues.quote: S -.->|view source shows| V[the HTML text]
issues.text: Order now matches the prose, and I can narrate the diagram. The dashed arrow is still the only dashed one, and the prose does not say why it looks different; I guess it means 'not part of what is drawn', but I am guessing.
issues.fix: Add one clause in the third paragraph: "(the dashed arrow in the diagram: view source reads the HTML text, not the tree)".

issues.quote: Start the lab with `scripts/up.sh` if it is not running
issues.text: Now I have a command, which fixes my round-1 problem. Two small doubts: I assume I run it from the root of the Đơn Hàng repository, and I do not know how to tell whether the lab is already running. I would just run it and see.
issues.fix: Write "Start the lab by running `scripts/up.sh` from the root of the Đơn Hàng repository (running it again is fine)" if re-running is safe; otherwise say how to check.

issues.quote: A second page would matter only when the address changed, but the page stayed the same and only part of it updated.
issues.text: I pick (a) easily. But explanations c and d rely on facts the context never states: it says the message appears 'after you click it', not that the address bar stayed the same or that no new page loaded. The explanation tells me something I was not given.
issues.fix: Add to the context: "...after you click it; the address bar does not change and the rest of the page stays as it was." Update vi to match.

issues.quote: False, because scripts add, remove and edit nodes, and the screen follows.
issues.text: The correct option repeats §6's 'a script in the page can add, remove and edit nodes, and each change shows on screen' almost word for word, so I can match it without thinking.
issues.fix: Reword in other terms, e.g. "False, because a script can change the tree in memory, and the browser redraws the page from it." Update vi to match.
